title: PAN Demands Investigation of AMLO’s Son; “What You’re About Is Hypocrisy,” Montiel Responds
author: SinEmbargo Newsroom
content:
_This article by the SinEmbargo newsroom originally appeared in the[August 16,
2026 edition of SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4855590/pan-exige-
investigar-a-hijo-de-amlo-lo-de-ustedes-es-la-hipocresia-responde-montiel/)._

**Mexico City, August 16 (SinEmbargo).—** Ariadna Montiel, national leader of
Morena, accused the PRIAN of "handing itself over to foreign interests," after
the National Action Party (PAN) held a press conference in which it demanded
that the Attorney General's Office (FGR) investigate Andrés Manuel López
Beltrán, son of former president Andrés Manuel López Obrador (AMLO), following
the cancellation of his US visa.

Through social media, Montiel stated that the PRIAN **" has decided to do what
conservatism has historically done: seek abroad the strength it does not have
in Mexico and hand itself over to foreign interests," out of its desperation
at not having the support of the Mexican people.**

The Morena leader responded directly to a post made by the national president
of the PAN, Jorge Romero Herrera, who reported on the conference the party
held to demand answers over alleged accusations against AMLO's son for
supposed ties to organized crime.

**" From the PAN, we will continue denouncing when power is used to protect
those who should be held accountable," the blue-and-white party leader wrote
in his message.**

> En la absoluta desesperación del
> [#PRIAN](https://x.com/hashtag/PRIAN?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw), porque
> sabe que no cuenta con el respaldo del pueblo y que volverá a perder en las
> urnas, porque durante décadas lo abandonaron. Ha decidido hacer lo que
> históricamente ha hecho el conservadurismo: buscar afuera la fuerza que no
> tiene en… <https://t.co/SEQ19J8VYX>
>
> -- Ariadna Montiel Reyes (@A_MontielR) [August 16,
> 2026](https://x.com/A_MontielR/status/2089118784460107924?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

In response, Ariadna Montiel pointed to the opposition's cynicism in speaking
of investigations, and mentioned the case of the PAN former governor Ernesto
Ruffo, detained for fuel theft (huachicol), for whom Acción Nacional came to
the defense and requested impunity despite the evidence against him.

> "What you're about is hypocrisy, betrayal of the country, corruption, and
> double standards. At the rate you're going, you should update your slogan:
> Betrayal, corruption, and huachicol,"
>
> Morena leader, Ariadna montien

## Mexico's Attorney General must investigate "Andy": PAN

During the conference held today by the PAN, Romero Herrera demanded that the
Mexican authorities clarify the reasons why the US government decided to
revoke the visa of Andrés Manuel López Beltrán, "Andy," in addition to
investigating an alleged link to "the fiscal huachicol scheme."

![The PAN holds a press conference demanding Morena clarify the visa
cancellation](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-16-pan-amlo-son-montiel-conference.jpg)At a
press conference, Acción Nacional (PAN) demanded that Morena clarify the
reason for the cancellation of Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's visa. Photo: PAN

"In the PAN, we demand, first, that they tell us why 'Andy's' visa. You may
say: 'one more person'; that's how they want to sell it, one visa fewer. No.
We are talking about the son of the former president of Mexico, and we have
serious doubts that it was revoked over some traffic violation or because he
stayed one or two extra days," said the party leader.

Likewise, he indicated that López Beltrán's conduct originates in his father's
"permissiveness." According to the PAN member, the former Morena Secretary of
Organization "is everything he is and was because of the permissiveness of
Andrés Manuel López Obrador. And let them not come tell us that the President
knew nothing."

Other key figures of Acción Nacional also took part in the conference, such as
its spokesman Jorge Triana; the Secretary of Communication of the party's
National Executive Committee (CEN), Max Cortázar; and federal Deputy Federico
Döring.
